solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Measure across diameter using compasses

indicators.note: to compass is to surround

parts.note: 'with' = using, as in 'cut with a knife'
d = diameter, the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson: measuring a circle across its diameter with a pair of compasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compasses' looks like the drawing instrument that belongs in the scene; here it is a verb meaning encloses, putting D inside WITH.
explanation.definitionFit: Width is a measurement taken across something.

clue.text: Sinister case of woman developing chill

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters are rearranged
the case of woman is its outside letters

explanation.surface: Something ominous about a woman coming down with a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: SINISTER plus WN (the outside of woman) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintriness is the cold quality of winter weather, a noun sense of chill.

clue.text: Complete time period, say

parts.note: to do a job is to complete it
t = time, the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Talk of a full stretch of time having passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time period' looks like one phrase; split it, and 'period' becomes the punctuation mark. The 'say' tells you a period is only one example of a dot.
explanation.definitionFit: A period, in American usage, is the full stop: a dot.

clue.text: Awful in hospital, but possibly free

parts.note: h = hospital, as on road signs
'or' offers an alternative, as 'but possibly' does
to rid is to free (of something)

explanation.surface: A grim hospital stay, though at least treatment might be free.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods at a free health service; 'free' is really the verb, as in ridding yourself of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something very unpleasant.

clue.text: Rat with cat coming over is first to disappear

indicators.note: 'is first' puts the word is ahead of the word for rat
'coming over' means the word for cat is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat, short for moggy
to rat on someone is to inform, or sing, to the police

explanation.surface: A rat meets a cat, and the rat is first to vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: Rat is a verb here, to inform on someone, not the animal; the cat is the British slang word short for moggy.
explanation.definitionFit: To go missing is to vanish or become lost, an idiom for disappearing.

clue.text: Illegal act I condemn involves kicking superstar

indicators.note: the phrase contains the answer inside it

parts.note: illeGAL ACT I COndemn

explanation.surface: Someone condemning an illegal act of kicking a star.
explanation.walkthrough: A galactico is a star footballer, from Real Madrid's big-money signings; 'kicking' makes the definition a football player rather than an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A galactico is a superstar footballer, a star who kicks a ball.

clue.text: Local chief agreed men should have married first

parts.note: m = married, as in genealogies
ay = yes, agreed
OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A local leader insisting men should have been married before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a small-town rule on marriage; 'men' is the army's other ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor is the chief civic officer of a town.

clue.text: Break down resistance of son frequently in court

parts.note: s = son, as in genealogies
straight synonym
to be up before the judge is to be in court

explanation.surface: A father despairing of a son who keeps ending up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' for 'in court' is a British idiom: someone 'up before the magistrates' is appearing in court.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from boxing and persuasion: you weaken an opponent's resistance before the real attack or request.

clue.text: Under canvas, you'd say one's not on it?

indicators.note: tells you to go by the sound when spoken

parts.note: under canvas = in a tent; one's = one has = I've

explanation.surface: A camper, asked where something is, replying that it isn't there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' must be read as 'one has', which gives I'VE; spoken quickly, 'in a tent I've' is inattentive.
explanation.definitionFit: A slangy definition: being 'on it' means alert and switched on, so not on it is its opposite.

clue.text: Bind grating that's twisted in the middle

indicators.note: something twisted is turned round on itself, so those letters face the other way
only the central letters RI are turned

parts.note: a grid is a grating; its middle RI turns to IR

explanation.surface: Tying up a metal grating that has buckled in the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the two middle letters of GRID swap round, leaving G and D in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in an old-fashioned register: girding a sword on means binding it round the waist.

clue.text: Of course you recover after turning brown

indicators.note: a word that turns round faces the other way

parts.note: tan is a brown; reversed to NAT
u = you, text-speak
a patient rallies, recovers

explanation.surface: Reassurance that you'll recover once you've gone brown in the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like advice after sunburn; 'turning brown' is really TAN turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally and of course both mean 'as expected'.

clue.text: Sudden blaze reported in particular faculty

indicators.note: tells you to go by the sound when spoken

parts.note: a flare is a sudden blaze of light

explanation.surface: A news item about a sudden fire at a university department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' suggests a university department; here it is a natural ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A flair is a special aptitude, a particular faculty for something.

clue.text: Funny wee fellow turning ten in October has run ahead

indicators.note: ahead puts the letter for run in front

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: turning means changing, so the letters of ten in October are rearranged

explanation.surface: A funny little man is turning ten this October and runs ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie Corbett was a famously short British comedian, half of The Two Ronnies.
explanation.definitionFit: Corbett was a comic known for his small stature, so a funny wee fellow describes him.

clue.text: Forecaster covering crazy techniques up with common sense

indicators.note: covering says the sense word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: nous is British slang for common sense

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: mad means crazy
arts are techniques or skills

explanation.surface: A predictor wraps wild methods in good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MADARTS into STRADAM, which NOUS goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostradamus was the French seer whose prophecies are still quoted as predictions.

clue.text: Notice a homo sapiens evolves, losing half its ancestry?

parts.note: an ad is a notice
man is the species homo sapiens

indicators.note: losing half removes the second half of the eight-letter word

parts.note: develops means evolves

explanation.surface: A note that humankind evolved, minus half its family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: DEVELOPS loses LOPS to leave DEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Adam and Eve are the first humans, the forebears of all mankind.

clue.text: Eat seconds of infected food and keep it down

indicators.note: seconds of takes the second letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Swallow the extra helpings of bad food and try not to throw up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep it down' sounds like holding food in; here it asks for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is British slang for food and, as a verb, for eating.

clue.text: Dud brew inn concocted, considerably overblown?

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up into something new

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A pub brewing duff beer and making great claims for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overblown' seems to mean exaggerated, but read literally it is having had too much wind blown over you, which chaps the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin that has been blown over by wind a great deal becomes windburned.

clue.text: Career over, walk in remote regions

indicators.note: in a down clue the word turns over, reading backwards

parts.note: to career is to speed along
to pace is to walk

explanation.surface: Someone whose career is over taking long walks in faraway places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career over' reads as retirement; 'career' is the verb to rush, so SPEED turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep space is the remote region beyond the solar system.

clue.text: Stretch tallest man on board for punishment

parts.note: a span is a stretch of time or distance
the king is the tallest chess piece

explanation.surface: The tallest man on a company board is stretched on the rack as punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' means on a chessboard, where the king is the tallest piece, not a company board.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a smacked bottom is one form of punishment, chiefly for children.

clue.text: Keep gambling habit on winning this?

definitions.meaning: the surface reading: sustaining an addiction to betting; really 'keep habit on', a habit being a garment
the game where winning is the only way to stay dressed

explanation.surface: Advice on sustaining a gambling addiction by winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' reads as an addiction; it is clothing, as a nun wears. In strip poker losers shed clothes, so only by winning do you keep your habit on.
explanation.definitionFit: In strip poker the losers remove clothing, so winners keep theirs on.

clue.text: Partners' concern when video changes hands?

indicators.note: L (left) is swapped for R (right)

parts.note: a video is a film; its L becomes R

explanation.surface: A partnership worried about who now owns a video.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' means business, and 'changes hands' is left to right, L to R.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm is a business concern, often run by partners.

clue.text: Bar closing for April, stagger home — poor kid

indicators.note: bar means except, so the closing letter is taken away

parts.note: to lurch is to stagger

indicators.note: the closing letter of April is its last

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A pub closes for April, and a poor child staggers home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub; it means 'except', removing L from LURCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a poor, often scruffy child of the streets.

clue.text: National Theatre distributes egg sandwiches, one nearly filling expert?

parts.note: to deal is to distribute
the NT, London's National Theatre, sits inside DEALSURGE
to egg on is to urge

indicators.note: 'nearly' cuts a letter off

parts.note: ONE is the word 'one' itself

explanation.surface: The National Theatre café handing out egg sandwiches, one almost overflowing.
explanation.walkthrough: The food picture makes 'egg' a noun and 'filling' a sandwich filling; egg is the verb urge, and the filling goes in a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: 'filling' suggests a sandwich, but the expert fills teeth.

clue.text: Courts cutting a hearing short

indicators.note: cutting a word short trims its end, here the final letter of trial
short says the word for hearing is missing its last letter

parts.note: a trial is a hearing in a court of law

explanation.surface: Courts abbreviating a legal hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus TRIA, which is TRIAL cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central courts in buildings, plural of atrium.

clue.text: Fast cloud in which odd bits of ash could drop

indicators.note: points to the odd-numbered letters
those odd letters are dropped, leaving the even ones

parts.note: a S h C o U l D: drop the odd letters

explanation.surface: A cloud blowing past a volcano, scattering ash.
explanation.walkthrough: The trap is taking the odd letters (AHOL); 'drop' says they are thrown away, leaving the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Scud is low, ragged cloud driven fast by the wind.

clue.text: Implement for easing locks one used for different purposes

parts.note: a comb untangles hair (locks)
I = one, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A burglar's tool for opening locks, with several uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests doors and burglars; they are locks of hair. A combi is a British term for a multi-purpose appliance, like a combi boiler.
explanation.definitionFit: Combi describes something combining several functions, used for different purposes.

clue.text: Henry half-way along on a rope within touching distance

parts.note: re = on, concerning
a cable is a heavy rope; H goes in its middle
h = henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry halfway along a rope, nearly within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a name; it is the physics unit, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe being close enough to touch.

clue.text: Tape with name cut off

indicators.note: a cut removes something, here the letter for name

parts.note: a band is a strip, a tape
n = name, removed from BAND

explanation.surface: Cutting a label with a name off a tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut off' looks like one phrasal verb; 'cut' works on the name and 'off' is the definition, as food goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the food sense: milk that has turned is spoiled.

clue.text: Authentically Asian spiciness reflected eastern style

parts.note: desi means authentically South Asian

indicators.note: a reflection runs the word backwards

parts.note: a tang is a sharp flavour; reversed to GNAT
e = eastern

explanation.surface: A curry described as genuinely Asian, its spice echoing an eastern style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' reads as a cooking style but is the verb, to call by a title. Desi, from Hindi, is common in British usage for South Asian things.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone something is to name them that, to designate them.

clue.text: Encouragement for one horse coming from the rear

indicators.note: the letters read from the back, reversed

parts.note: e.g. = for example, for one
a dun is a greyish-brown horse

explanation.surface: Urging a horse on from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' gives EG, for example, and a dun is a horse of dull brown colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a gentle push towards doing something is a mild form of encouragement.
